newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BATISTUTA EARNS DRAW FOR FIORENTINA AT BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BATISTUTA EARNS DRAW FOR FIORENTINA AT BARCELONA.

text.p: A moment of inspiration from Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta ensured a well-deserved 1-1 draw for Fiorentina at Barcelona in Thursday's European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal first leg.
With over an hour on the clock, it had looked as if the Italians might have to go home with a 1-0 defeat after Miguel Angel Nadal had headed Barcelona ahead just before the break.
But Batistuta pounced after controlling the ball superbly on the edge of the area and gave Barcelona keeper Vitor Baia no chance with a fiercely struck shot.

Batistuta had led a surprisingly positive Italian side from the start, combining well throughout the game with Oliveira, Giulio Falcone and Rui Costa, who seemed to revel down the flanks in the wide open spaces of the Camp Nou stadium.
The first clear chance of the evening fell to Batistuta in the 15th minute.
The Argentine headed wide after slipping clear of Fernando Couto, the Portuguese international who marked him tightly throughout the game.

The visitors squandered several other chances, and were made to pay for their mistakes just before halftime when Miguel Angel Nadal outclimbed the defence in a set-piece move from the right and glanced his header just inside the far post.
Barcelona enjoyed their only spell of domination at the beginning of the second half but were unable to capitalise as both Giovanni and Stoichkov wasted opportunities.
Barcelona fans also saw a promising move stopped by the referee for offside on the stroke of the hour.
The Italians broke swiftly out of defence and were able to stand back in admiration as Batistuta picked up a long pass, chested down the ball and blasted home the equaliser.
The goal breathed new life into a game that had been hit by constant stoppages.
Moments later Barcelona's Luis Figo found room down the left but saw Guillermo Amor shoot high after doing well to pull the ball back.
Ronaldo, the Brazilian striker who is thought to interest a number of Italian clubs, had a a quiet game but gave the visitors a scare when he beat his man and brushed a post with a left-foot shot.
With former Parma player Hristo Stoichkov having a poor game Bobby Robson brought on Juan Pizzi for the last quarter hour.
But it was Fiorentina who had looked likely to have the last word until the referee ended a dangerous counter-attack by blowing the final whistle.
Batistuta will miss the second leg after receiving a yellow card for colliding with Roger Garcia in the opening minutes.
Barcelona's Gheorghe Popescu, who was booked in the final minute, is in the same boat.
"The Italians always defend well, and tonight was no exception," said Popescu afterwards.

But Barcelona coach Bobby Robson will welcome back playmakers Ivan de la Pena and Josep Guardiola from suspension, and hopes to have overlapping full-backs Sergi Barjuan and Luis Enrique Martinez fit again.
